# Disagreement Log — Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 16

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Summary
Total disagreements: 31

---

## Disagreements

**v. 1** — "creatures" (EMET) vs. "vermin" (LOGOS) vs. "vermin" (PNEUMA). Both translate κτηνῶν. LOGOS/PNEUMA's "vermin" is more specific and contextually appropriate.

**v. 2** — "benefited your people" (EMET) vs. "treated your people kindly" (LOGOS) vs. "turned the tables entirely" (PNEUMA). PNEUMA interprets too freely. LOGOS preferred.

**v. 2** — "preparing for their craving a delicacy of taste" (EMET) vs. "to satisfy their craving you prepared a delicacy to delight the palate" (LOGOS) vs. "satisfying their craving with something choice and delicious" (PNEUMA). LOGOS structure preferred.

**v. 3** — "loathsome creatures produced among them" (EMET) vs. "loathsome creatures sent among them" (LOGOS) vs. "disgusting creatures swarming around them" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 3** — "a delicacy of food" (EMET) vs. "extraordinary fare" (LOGOS) vs. "extraordinary delicacies" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 4** — "inescapable want" (EMET) vs. "inescapable destitution" (LOGOS) vs. "relentless deprivation" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 5** — "fierce rage" (EMET) vs. "fierce wrath" (LOGOS) vs. "savage fury" (PNEUMA). Greek θυμός = anger/wrath/passion. LOGOS preferred.

**v. 5** — "bites of crooked serpents" (EMET) vs. "bites of writhing serpents" (LOGOS) vs. "bites of writhing serpents" (LOGOS/PNEUMA agree). "writhing" preferred over "crooked."

**v. 5** — "your wrath did not continue to the end" (EMET) vs. "your anger did not persist to the end" (LOGOS) vs. "your anger did not burn all the way to the end" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 6** — "as a warning they were troubled" (EMET) vs. "as a chastening warning" (LOGOS) vs. "a corrective shock" (PNEUMA). SOPHIA: "as a corrective warning."

**v. 6** — "sign of salvation" (EMET) vs. "token of salvation" (LOGOS) vs. "sign of salvation" (EMET/PNEUMA). Greek σύμβολον = symbol/token/sign. LOGOS's "token" preferred as more precise.

**v. 8** — "persuaded our enemies" (EMET) vs. "convinced our enemies" (LOGOS) vs. "proved to our enemies" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 8** — "delivers from every evil" (EMET) vs. "rescues from every evil" (LOGOS) vs. "delivers from every evil" (PNEUMA). LOGOS/EMET tie; SOPHIA: "rescues."

**v. 9** — "killed by the bites of locusts and flies" (LOGOS, PNEUMA) vs. "killed by the bites of locusts and flies" (EMET). All agree on substance; LOGOS structure adopted.

**v. 11** — "your oracles" (EMET) vs. "your words" (LOGOS) vs. "your promises" (PNEUMA). Greek λόγια = oracles/utterances. LOGOS preferred.

**v. 11** — "your kindness" (EMET) vs. "your loving-kindness" (LOGOS) vs. "your goodness" (PNEUMA). Greek χρηστότητα = kindness/goodness. LOGOS preferred.

**v. 13** — "authority over life and death" (EMET) vs. "power over life and death" (LOGOS) vs. "power over life and death" (PNEUMA). LOGOS/PNEUMA agree on "power."

**v. 13** — "lead down to the gates of Hades and bring up again" (EMET) vs. "lead down to the gates of Hades and lead back up again" (LOGOS) vs. "lead down to the gates of death" (PNEUMA — omits return). LOGOS preferred; PNEUMA's omission is a loss.

**v. 16** — "unusual rains" (EMET) vs. "extraordinary rains" (LOGOS) vs. "freak downpours" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 17** — "most extraordinary of all" (EMET) vs. "most marvelous of all" (LOGOS) vs. "strangest thing of all" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 17** — "the world is the champion of the righteous" (EMET) vs. "the world champions the cause of the righteous" (LOGOS) vs. "the whole creation takes sides for the righteous" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 20** — "food of angels" — all three agree. LOGOS structure adopted.

**v. 20** — "without their labor" (EMET) vs. "without their toil" (LOGOS) vs. "without any labour on their part" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 21** — "your sustenance demonstrated your sweetness" (EMET) vs. "your provision showed forth your sweetness" (LOGOS) vs. "your nourishment revealed your sweetness" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 22** — "snow and ice endured fire without melting" (EMET) vs. "snow and ice withstood fire without melting" (LOGOS) vs. "snow and ice endured fire without melting" (EMET/PNEUMA). LOGOS "withstood" preferred.

**v. 23** — "fire forgot its own power" — all three agree on this striking image; no dispute.

**v. 24** — "serving you who made it" (EMET) vs. "serving you its Maker" (LOGOS) vs. "it serves you, its Maker" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 25** — "transforming itself into all things" (EMET) vs. "taking on all forms" (LOGOS) vs. "took on every form" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 26** — "the production of crops" (EMET) vs. "the various crops" (LOGOS) vs. "the variety of the harvest" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 28** — "hasten before the sun to give thanks to you" (EMET) vs. "rise before the sun to give you thanks" (LOGOS) vs. "greet you before sunrise" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 29** — "winter frost" (EMET) vs. "wintry frost" (LOGOS) vs. "frost in winter" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 29** — "run off like useless water" (EMET) vs. "flow away like water without use" (LOGOS) vs. "drains off like water that no one needs" (PNEUMA). SOPHIA: "flow away like water that serves no purpose."
